claim: Audio is a small placeholder set — hit, cast and reward cues only. No music yet.
evidence: Music ships and plays. assets/audio/music/ holds 12 looping tracks: music_title, music_combat, music_forge, music_warren, music_map, music_constellation, and six music_arena_<source> tracks. They are copied by the **\*.wav Content rule in src/IdleXIdle.Game/IdleXIdle.Game.csproj, and the last publish has them (build/release/IDLExIDLE-win64/assets/audio/music). src/IdleXIdle.Game/Game1.cs:5052-5067 (UpdateMusic) picks a track for each screen and region and calls _sound.PlayMusic; it runs every frame from Latch (Game1.cs:5007). Settings has a MUSIC VOLUME slider (Game1.cs:9373), default 50 (DisplaySettings.cs:224). There are 31 sound effects, not three kinds: 8 in assets/audio/combat and 23 in assets/audio/ui (click, nav, error, equip, train, weave, bind, forge, upgrade, reroll, gem, salvage, chest open/rare, reveal tick, levelup, conquer, deepen, dispatch, shield). The music was added in f4b79d0 and 3ca8bf5 (2026-08-14), before this doc was written (2026-09-08).
replacement: - **Sound is simple placeholder work.** A program made every sound; none is final. There are about 30 sound effects (hits, casts, bosses, the Forge, chests, rewards, menus). There is looping music: one track each for the title, the Forge, the Warren, the Map and the Traits screen, and one track for each region, which plays during the hunt and on the other screens. Change the volume of each in Settings (EFFECTS VOLUME and MUSIC VOLUME).
note: Confirmed. assets/audio/music has 12 WAVs, the csproj copies assets/audio/**/*.wav, Game1.UpdateMusic runs from Latch every frame and calls _sound.PlayMusic, and Settings has EFFECTS VOLUME and MUSIC VOLUME sliders (Game1.cs:9394/9396). There are 31 sound effects (8 combat + 23 ui), and assets/audio/README.md says scripts synthesised all of them. One problem with the replacement: 'a looping music track for each main screen' overstates it. Only the title, Forge, Warren, Traits (music_constellation) and Map have their own tracks. Every other screen (Gear, Build, Mastery, Training, Vault, Roster) and the hunt plays the current region's track. The six region tracks match the six region themes (Nature, Machine, Shadow, Body, Mind, Spirit).

claim: Mouse only. Left-click chooses, right-click opens an item's menu, the wheel scrolls any column that overflows. The left rail switches screens.
evidence: The game has many keyboard controls. Game1.cs:4141 F1 = help sheet, 4142 F10 = settings, 4147 M = DISPATCHES. Game1.cs:4336-4349 loop over the rail hotkeys defined at Game1.cs:10733-10745 (H C V B E K F A W P R). Game1.cs:4366 L = expedition log. Game1.cs:4015-4033: Esc opens Settings, or first closes an open panel. Game1.cs:3954: on the title screen, Esc quits the game. The F1 sheet lists the keys (Game1.cs:10578-10593). The Settings footer says 'EVERY KEY IS LISTED IN HELP (F1) · KEYS CANNOT BE REBOUND YET' (Game1.cs:9413). The F1 sheet has no mouse button; the ? button starts a screen tour instead. The right mouse button does three different things: it opens the item menu on GEAR (GearScreen.cs:714-735), sells a gem in the FORGE (ForgeScreen.cs:2271), and gives a node back on MASTERY (MasteryScreen.cs:1326-1340). On MASTERY the wheel zooms (MasteryScreen.cs:1277-1280) and dragging moves the tree. Rail tiles stay chained shut until the matching Unlocks gate opens (Unlocks.cs:137-199). The settings gear sits at the top right (Game1.cs:8858). No file in src/IdleXIdle.Game references GamePad, so there is no controller support.
replacement:
You can play with the mouse alone. Left-click chooses. Right-click opens an item's menu on the GEAR screen, sells a gem in the FORGE, and gives a point back on the MASTERY tree. The wheel scrolls any list that is too long. On the MASTERY tree the wheel zooms, and you drag to move the tree. The rail on the left switches screens. A tile with a chain on it is a screen that is not open yet; it opens as you play. The gear icon at the top right opens Settings.

The keyboard is optional. Press F1 for the list of keys. Esc opens Settings (on the title screen, Esc quits the game). F10 also opens Settings, M opens your letters (DISPATCHES), and L opens the expedition log. Each screen has a letter: H hunt, C gear, V training, B build, E mastery, K vault, F forge, A warren, W map, P traits, R roster. You cannot change the keys yet, and there is no controller support yet. Nothing is timed and nothing needs fast reactions.
note: Confirmed. 'Mouse only' is wrong. The code handles F1, F10, M, L and Esc; the rail letters H C V B E K F A W P R go through OpenNav; there is also T (weave, Game1.cs:4394) and D (deepen, MapScreen.cs:705). On the title screen Esc calls Exit(). Right-click does three things: it opens the item menu on GEAR (GearScreen.cs:714), calls Sell on a gem row in the FORGE (ForgeScreen.cs:2271, which may ask first), and gives a node back on MASTERY (MasteryScreen.cs:1326). On MASTERY the wheel zooms the tree and dragging moves it. Since the 2026-09-09 change in Reveal.cs, every rail tile is drawn and locked ones are chained. The settings gear is at the top right (PageRight). No source file mentions GamePad. One wording fix: the F1 sheet does not list every key (T, D, Enter and Space are missing), so 'Press F1 to see every key' should be softened.

claim: The window opens at 1920×1080 and the UI SCALE setting (100 / 125 / 150 %) is a density profile
evidence: On first launch the game is FULLSCREEN, not a 1920x1080 window. DisplaySettings.cs:224 sets the default to new(DisplayMode.Fullscreen, new WindowSize(1920, 1080), ...), and 1920x1080 is only the size WINDOWED mode falls back to. Game1.cs:1013-1020 loads these preferences and applies them. Game1.cs:7993-7997 sizes fullscreen to the monitor (display.Width/Height), using soft fullscreen (HardwareModeSwitch=false, Game1.cs:896). The window size is clamped to fit the desktop (Game1.cs:7980, Display.NearestOffered). The page is always a 1920x1080 canvas, scaled to fit with letterbox bars (DisplaySettings.cs PresentFit). UI SCALE has four settings, not three: DisplaySettings.cs:174 UiScaleSteps = {100, 125, 150, 0}, where 0 means AUTO. The Settings caption reads 'AUTO PICKS 125% IN A SMALL WINDOW' (Game1.cs:9362-9364). A fresh prefs file starts at 100.
replacement: Unzip and run `IDLExIDLE.exe`. It is self-contained: no runtime, no installer, no dependencies. The first launch opens full screen, at your monitor's size. To play in a window, open Settings and set MODE to WINDOWED, then pick a WINDOW SIZE (1920 × 1080 at first, or the nearest size that fits your screen). The game is always drawn as one 1920 × 1080 page, scaled to fit, with dark bars if your screen has a different shape. UI SCALE (100 %, 125 %, 150 % or AUTO; 100 % at first) is a density setting: the page stays the same size, and the text, rows and buttons grow. AUTO picks 125 % in a small window.
note: Confirmed. DisplaySettings.Default is DisplayMode.Fullscreen with a windowed fallback of 1920x1080, and Game1 applies the loaded preferences at startup. ApplyDisplay sizes Fullscreen to the monitor, and Windowed is clamped by Display.NearestOffered. UiScaleSteps = {100,125,150,0}, where 0 is AUTO. ResolveUiScale picks 125 when the view is narrower than 1600 px, and the Settings caption says 'AUTO PICKS 125% IN A SMALL WINDOW'. A missing prefs file gives UiScalePercent 100. The Settings labels MODE, WINDOWED and WINDOW SIZE are real. The replacement is accurate.

claim: The same id is the itch.io build version, the BUILD line in Settings and on the title screen, and part of every feedback code (example 0.1.0-alpha+a6fc3c9); the pre-alpha builds had only the commit id.
evidence: These three places show the commit id at three different lengths. tools/publish/itch_push.sh:35 uses SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD), which gives 7 characters in this repo ('a6fc3c9'), and line 38 builds USERVERSION from it. src/IdleXIdle.Core/Persistence/BuildStamp.cs:31 cuts the Short stamp to sha[..8], and Settings (Game1.cs:9457) and the title screen (Game1.cs:10411) print that 8-character form. The Release Core dll carries 0.1.0-alpha+a6fc3c9d7d17eb74..., so the game shows 'BUILD 0.1.0-alpha+a6fc3c9d' while itch.io shows '0.1.0-alpha+a6fc3c9'. The feedback code carries BuildStamp.Full, the full 40-character id (Game1.cs:1623). On the pre-alpha builds, only the itch.io version was the bare commit id. The game itself printed '1.0.0+<8 chars>' (Directory.Build.props comment; the old publish build/release/IDLExIDLE-win64/IdleXIdle.Core.dll carries '1.0.0+db52574a...'). The simplest fix is in code: change itch_push.sh:35 to `git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD`. That makes the doc's 'same id' sentence true, with the example changed to 8 characters.
replacement: - **Alpha.** The version is `0.1.0-alpha` plus the commit id. The itch.io build version uses a short form of the id (for example `0.1.0-alpha+a6fc3c9`), the BUILD line in Settings and on the title screen shows its first 8 characters (`0.1.0-alpha+a6fc3c9d`), and every feedback code carries the full id. All three start the same way, so a tester's report and the build page agree. (On the pre-alpha builds, the itch.io version was only the commit id, and the game showed `1.0.0+` and the commit id.)
note: Confirmed. itch_push.sh uses `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, which gives 7 characters here (a6fc3c9; core.abbrev is not set). BuildStamp.Short cuts the id to 8 characters and is what Settings and the title screen print. The feedback code carries BuildStamp.Full. The Release Core dll carries 0.1.0-alpha+a6fc3c9d7d17..., so the game shows ...+a6fc3c9d while itch.io shows ...+a6fc3c9. The old publish's dll reads 1.0.0+db52574a..., and the old script pushed the bare sha. Since this is a doc-only fix, I give the wording that is true without a code change. It avoids a fixed '7' because git's short length grows with the repo. If itch_push.sh is changed to --short=8, use the agent's first replacement instead.

claim: To evaluate from a clean start, close the game and delete (or rename) that folder — the next launch begins a fresh account. save.bak ... is restored automatically if a save is ever truncated.
evidence: The claim is true, but it leaves out three things a tester needs. (1) Deleting the folder also resets display and sound settings: display.txt lives in the same folder (DisplaySettings.cs:141-143, SaveFile.AppDataFolderName). (2) There is a trap for anyone who played a build from before 2026-09-08. On a launch that finds no save, SaveFile.cs:53-58 calls SaveStore.AdoptOnce (SaveStore.cs:60-80), which MOVES %LOCALAPPDATA%\ResonanceHunter\save.json into the new folder. So a tester who deletes IDLExIDLE while an old ResonanceHunter save still exists gets the old game back, not a fresh one. (3) There is an in-game reset: Settings > DANGER ZONE > START A NEW GAME. It needs two clicks ('SURE? THIS DELETES YOUR SAVE — CLICK AGAIN', Game1.cs:9420-9441). It deletes the save, sets save.bak aside as save.bak-pre-reset-<time> (Game1.cs:1661-1669), and keeps display settings. The save.bak restore is real, and it covers any unreadable file, not only a cut-off one. Game1.cs:1065-1075 moves the bad file aside as save.corrupt-<time>.json (SaveStore.cs:162, 233-245), loads save.bak, and writes it back. The path %LOCALAPPDATA%\IDLExIDLE\save.json is correct (SaveFile.cs:25, SaveStore.cs:30).
replacement: **To evaluate from a clean start,** open Settings and use DANGER ZONE → START A NEW GAME (click it twice). This deletes the save and starts a fresh account; your display and sound settings stay. Or close the game and delete (or rename) the folder above. This also resets your display and sound settings, because they are kept in the same folder (`display.txt`). If you ever played a build from before 8 September 2026, also delete `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ResonanceHunter`. If you do not, the next launch moves that old save into the new folder and loads it. `save.bak` beside the save is the previous good save. If the save file is damaged, the game loads `save.bak` by itself and keeps the damaged file as `save.corrupt-<time>.json`.
note: Confirmed. display.txt is in the same IDLExIDLE folder (DisplaySettings.PrefsPath). SaveFile.Dir calls SaveStore.AdoptOnce, which MOVES the files from %LOCALAPPDATA%\ResonanceHunter when the new folder has no save.json. itch builds from before f836ff4 (2026-09-08) saved to ResonanceHunter, and this doc is shipped as the build's README, so a tester who only played those builds and deletes the new folder gets the old game back. The in-game path is real: DANGER ZONE, START A NEW GAME, then an armed 'SURE? THIS DELETES YOUR SAVE — CLICK AGAIN'. StartNewGame calls PreserveBackupAside and TryDelete and does not touch display prefs. The corrupt-file path moves the bad file aside as save.corrupt-<time>, loads save.bak and writes it back. The replacement is accurate. The legacy advice is conservative (it matters only while the old folder still holds a save.json), which is fine.

claim: Six regions and ten champions are in; the deep ladder past the sixth region is generated rather than authored.
evidence: Six regions (Regions.cs:80-123) and ten champions (CharacterRoster.cs:46-235) are correct. There is nothing 'past the sixth region', generated or authored. Once every region is conquered, World.CanDeepenCorruption (Regions.cs:197) opens a DEEPER button on the MAP (MapScreen.cs:1162, key D at MapScreen.cs:705). It raises the whole world through 5 named corruption tiers, capped at CorruptionScaling.cs:17 MaxTier = 5, with names from CorruptionLook.cs:20-27 (STIRRING ... ABYSSAL). These tiers reuse the same six regions with more enemy health and more reward (CorruptionScaling.cs:22-27). Waves past 20 in a region continue with the same wave machinery (Checkpoints.cs:9-12, OVERWAVE). A tester reading 'ten champions are in' may also expect all ten at once. Only THE SEEKER is open at the start (CharacterRoster.cs:62). Four champions join on the conquest of regions 2-5: cinderworks, umbral_reach, marrow_wastes, still_archive (CharacterRoster.cs:82/96/112/124, checked against conquered ids at CharacterState.cs:73). Five join through quests (CharacterRoster.cs:143/165/190/215/233). A separate problem I noticed but did not trace through the host: the ROSTER opens at the FIRST conquest with 'Another hunter joined you. Meet them.' (Unlocks.cs:199, 225, 249), but no champion is tied to the first region, Verdant Hollow. The second hunter arrives only when Cinderworks is conquered.
replacement: - **Alpha content depth.** Six regions and ten champions are in. You start with one champion, THE SEEKER. Four more join when you conquer the second, third, fourth and fifth regions, and the last five join through quests. There is no seventh region yet. After all six regions are conquered, the MAP lets you make the whole world harder in five steps (CORRUPTION 1 to 5). Each step uses the same six regions, with tougher enemies and bigger rewards. Past wave 20, a region keeps sending waves that grow stronger.
note: Confirmed. Regions.All has exactly six regions, and nothing comes after them. After all six are conquered, CanDeepenCorruption allows up to CorruptionScaling.MaxTier = 5 tiers. Each tier uses the same regions with more enemy health (x(1+0.6t)) and more reward (x(1+t)), shown as 'CORRUPTION n / 5 · NAME'. Past wave 20 the waves continue (OVERWAVE). Roster: SEEKER is the only champion at the start. ANVIL, CHORUS, METRONOME and UNBROKEN unlock on the conquest of cinderworks, umbral_reach, marrow_wastes and still_archive (regions 2-5), checked in CharacterState.Refresh. The other five come from quests. The doc's 'generated rather than authored' could loosely describe the formula-scaled tiers, but 'past the sixth region' tells a reader there is content beyond region six, which is false. The replacement is accurate. The side note is also real: Unlocks.cs opens the Roster at the first conquest and says 'Another hunter joined you', but no champion is tied to Verdant Hollow.

claim: Known, non-blocking (the list as a whole: content depth, audio, Forge at 150 %)
evidence: The list dates from 2026-09-08 (commits d1f5683/f836ff4). It misses issues open in this build. (a) Texture memory: production/session-state/active.md:18 says 'A live fight holds ~679 MB of textures against the 512 MB working ceiling (boot 439 MB)'. Commit 239f890 measured one fight at about 671 MB. AssetLibrary.cs:33 says 'Nothing is evicted', so memory grows as more regions, bosses and champions are seen. (b) Keys cannot be changed: Game1.cs:9413 'KEYS CANNOT BE REBOUND YET'. (c) No controller support: no GamePad reference in src/IdleXIdle.Game. (d) If it is not fixed first, the ROSTER first-conquest message (see the content-depth finding) is a visible copy error. The Forge-at-150% item itself is still accurate: the bag, item and compare columns scroll (ForgeScreen.cs:1404-1409), and d1f5683 accepts the density as designed.
replacement:
- **Memory.** A fight holds about 680 MB of graphics memory (textures), about 440 MB at start-up. That is above the 512 MB the project budgets for. Art loads the first time it is needed and is not released during a session, so the figure grows as you visit more regions and meet more bosses and champions. With every piece of art loaded, it would be about 2.2 GB.
- **Keys and controllers.** You cannot change the keys yet, and there is no controller support yet.
note: The gaps are real. production/session-state/active.md lists about 679 MB of textures in a fight against the 512 MB working ceiling (439 MB at boot). Commit 239f890 gives 671 MB, and says loading all the art up front took 2247 MB. AssetLibrary says 'Nothing is evicted'. The Settings footer says 'KEYS CANNOT BE REBOUND YET', and no source mentions GamePad even though technical-preferences lists full gamepad support as a target. A publisher would ask about both. The Forge-at-150% item is still valid. I tightened the memory wording: it gives the upper bound and says 'textures' plainly.

claim: Vows — a promise sworn onto a skill that pays only while the promise is kept.
evidence: A vow is a promise about the whole BUILD, not about one skill, and it pays on every skill. Vows.cs:33-52 says 'What a Vow demands of the BUILD', with demands like SingleStyle, NoKeystone and SlotLeftBare (Vows.cs:53-96). PlayerLoadout.cs:122-140 makes vow capacity a build-level number, and PlayerLoadout.cs:190 counts distinct sworn vows. The Build screen hint reads 'A PROMISE KEPT IS PAID ON EVERY SKILL' (LoadoutScreen.cs:2183). A vow is found by play, not bought: 'A VOW REVEALS ITSELF WHEN YOU KEEP ITS RULE WITHOUT IT' (same line), and VowProof is at Vows.cs:103-120. Some vows are StaticCost: 'Always active, always costing you something' (Vows.cs:28). The number you can hold is 0 before wave 5, then 1, then 2 after 2 conquests and 3 after 4 (Unlocks.cs VowCapacity). The slot a vow is 'sworn at' is only where the choice is recorded (PlayerLoadout.cs:339-349).
replacement: - **Vows** — a promise about your whole build, for example "every skill is the same style" or "leave one gear slot empty". While the build keeps the promise, every skill hits harder; break it and the vow pays nothing. Two vows have no rule: they always pay, and always cost you (you take more damage, or have less health). The first vow is given to you. Most others appear after you clear 10 to 20 waves keeping their rule without them. You can swear one vow from wave 5, and a second and third after more conquests.
note: Confirmed. SoloBattle.cs:830-835 says 'A Vow is a promise about the whole BUILD'. Vows.CombinedFactor sums the kept vows' bonuses under one ceiling and applies them to every skill's damage. The slot only records where the vow was sworn (PlayerLoadout.SetVow). VowCapacity is 0 before wave 5, then 1, 2 at 2 conquests, and 3 at 4. The replacement has two errors. (1) 'You find a vow by keeping its rule once without it' is not right: VOW OF COMPLETION is simply given (VowProof.Granted), most vows appear after 10-20 waves cleared while keeping the rule unsworn (ProofWaves), and the two StaticCost vows (FRAGILITY, RECKLESS OFFERING) have no rule; they always pay and always cost you. (2) 'While you keep the promise' does not fit those two static vows.

claim: THE THORNWALL answers what strikes it. The innate is identity, not a number to allocate.
evidence: The sentence sits where the champion's innate rule is described (the ANVIL sentence before it describes the ANVIL's innate, DEADWEIGHT, correctly: CharacterRoster.cs:73-82, DeadweightShare = 0.33f). But THE THORNWALL's innate is REPRISAL: 'Every hit you take does less. Every trap you set does more.' (CharacterRoster.cs:174-186: FlatDamageReduction 6, DamageTaken 0.90, SNARE power x1.35). The part that 'answers what strikes it' is its signature skill NARROWS, a Reaction on Bitten (SkillCatalogue.cs:1034-1040). A reviewer checking the innate would call the sentence wrong.
replacement: THE THORNWALL takes less damage from every hit and makes its traps stronger, and its signature skill answers every bite with a hit of its own. The innate is identity, not a number to allocate.
note: Confirmed. THORNWALL's innate is REPRISAL: FlatDamageReduction 6, DamageTaken 0.90 and SNARE power x1.35 ('Every hit you take does less. Every trap you set does more.'). The 'answers what strikes it' behaviour is the signature NARROWS (Reaction, On: Bitten), and the doc places the sentence right after the ANVIL's innate. One nit in the replacement: NARROWS hits 'the enemy in front' (Targets: 1), which is not necessarily the enemy that bit, so 'hits back at whatever bites it' is slightly off.

claim: every clear pays Gleam and hauls loot
evidence: An ordinary wave pays Gleam plus exactly ONE crafting material (WaveSpoils.cs:44 UnitsPerWave = 1). From wave 5 it also has a 2.5 % chance of a Forge chart (WaveSpoils.cs:61, 69). Items come only from boss chests, and every 5th wave is a boss (WaveModel.cs:228 BossEvery = 5). The game's own F1 sheet says 'EACH WAVE IT CLEARS PAYS GLEAM AT ONCE. EVERY 5TH WAVE IS A BOSS, AND ONLY A BOSS DROPS A CHEST.' (Game1.cs:10614). A tester who reads 'hauls loot' will expect items from every wave. The next sentence ('Twenty waves conquer a region and open the next') is correct: Checkpoints.cs:29 ConquestWave = 20, and Regions.cs World.Conquer opens Regions.Next.
replacement: 1. **Hunt.** A descent runs continuously: waves arrive, the champion fights, and every wave it clears pays Gleam and one crafting material. Every fifth wave is a boss. Only bosses drop chests of items, and about one boss in five drops one (your first boss always does). Cooldowns carry from one wave to the next, so a descent is one long fight rather than a series of rounds. Twenty waves conquer a region and open the next.
note: Confirmed. Game1.cs:7260-7290 pays each cleared wave Gleam plus WaveSpoils.Roll: exactly 1 unit of material, and from wave 5 a 2.5% chance of a Forge chart. Items come only from chests, and chests come only from bosses. The replacement's 'only a boss drops a chest' reads as if every boss drops one. DropBossChest rolls ChestTuning.DropChance = 0.20 ('most bosses give nothing'). The first boss always gives the Welcome Gift chest. Corrected below.

claim: Progress is credited while the game is closed, up to a cap that grows with the Warren.
evidence: The claim is true, but it has no numbers, and 'progress' is broader than what is paid. OfflineCamp.cs:38-50 sets BaseHours = 2, HoursPerFacilityLevel = 0.1 (6 minutes), MaxHours = 12, BaseEfficiency = 0.30 and MaxEfficiency = 0.60. Game1.cs:1361-1389 pays the champion's offline Gleam from the start, with camp = null, which means 2 hours at 30 %. The Warren's own production is paid only once the Warren is open, after the first conquest (Game1.cs:1361-1370; Unlocks.cs Warren gate). Time away pays GLEAM only: no chests, no materials from the hunt, no records, no skill levels (OfflineHunt.cs:28-32). A reviewer would ask 'what cap?' and 'what progress?'.
replacement: While the game is closed, your champion keeps earning Gleam, at 30 % of what live play pays. A new account is paid for up to 2 hours away. After your first conquest the Warren opens: each Warren level you buy adds 6 minutes (up to 12 hours) and raises the share (up to 60 %), and the Warren's own work is paid for the same time. Time away gives no chests, no records and no skill levels.
note: Confirmed. OfflineCamp has BaseHours 2, +0.1 h per facility level bought, MaxHours 12, BaseEfficiency 0.30, +0.003 per level, and MaxEfficiency 0.60. Game1.cs:1361-1389 passes camp = null (2 h, 30%) until the Warren gate opens, and the Warren produces only once it is open, for the same held seconds. OfflineHunt credits only Gleam: no chests, materials, records, quests or skill levels. 'Progress is credited' suggests more than Gleam, so the added detail is worth having. The replacement is accurate. It could also mention that the next live descent starts from the wave reached while away, capped at the region's best depth (Game1.cs:1404-1409), but that is optional.

claim: Traits — discovered by playing a style rather than bought, and read off the fight itself.
evidence: 'Not bought' is correct: there are 26 traits in TraitCatalogue.cs:196-468, each woken by a hidden counter crossing a number (TraitDiscovery.cs:66-80, TraitRule at TraitCatalogue.cs:63). But the counters are mostly not 'a style'. Some are fight facts, such as HeavyHits 1,000 (TraitCatalogue.cs:206) and UntouchedWaves 500 (line 463). Some are account facts that do not come from the fight: SetsCompleted 2 for THE MATCHED SUIT (line 411), RegionsConquered 4 for HOMEGROUND (line 424), RegionsMastered 2 (line 433), and WallStreak 3, meaning three falls in a row in one region, for WHAT KILLED YOU (line 450). The in-game gate reads 'Discover a characteristic by how you fight' (Unlocks.cs:224).
replacement: - **Traits** — 26 of them, never bought. Each one wakes when you have done something often enough: landing heavy hits, breaking shields, keeping vows, completing gear sets, conquering regions, even losing three descents in a row in one region to the same kind of enemy. The rule behind each trait stays hidden until it wakes.
note: Partly confirmed. TraitCatalogue has 26 traits, each woken by a hidden counter reaching a number (TraitDiscovery: 'Hidden from the player'), and none is bought. But 'playing a style' clashes with the doc's own STYLE term (HAMMER, VOLLEY...), and no trait counts a Style. Several counters are not fight facts: SetsCompleted 2, RegionsConquered 4, RegionsMastered 2 and RunsWithVowKept 40. So the doc's generalisation misleads. One nit in the replacement: WallStreak means three descents in a row in one region that ended against the same kind of creature, not 'the same enemy'.

claim: you decide what the champion becomes: which four skills it weaves
evidence: Four is only the maximum. A champion starts with ONE skill slot, holding its signature. The other slots open with mastery points and depth: wave 5, wave 12, then the first conquest (Unlocks.cs:311-318 SkillSlots; PlayerLoadout.cs:95 MaxSkills = 4). The F1 sheet shows the live count, not a fixed four (Game1.cs:10563).
replacement: you decide what the champion becomes: which skills it weaves (one at first, up to four), which style it commits to, which promises it swears, and what it wears.
note: Confirmed. Unlocks.SkillSlots starts at 1 (the champion's signature, from PlayerLoadout.Starter) and adds a slot at wave 5, wave 12 and the first conquest, each also needing mastery points. PlayerLoadout.MaxSkills is 4, and the F1 sheet shows the live SkillCapacity. A reviewer starting fresh sees one slot, so 'which four skills' will look wrong. The replacement is small and accurate.
